         junit_log_passing_tests = False
 
 
+.. confval:: junit_output_limit
+
+    .. versionadded:: 8.5
+
+    If ``junit_logging != "no"``, limits the number of Unicode characters kept,
+    per test and per section (captured stdout, stderr and log), when writing
+    captured output to the JUnit XML file. This is useful to prevent CI report
+    uploads from becoming huge when tests print or log a lot.
+
+    The limit applies independently to each section's own raw content, before
+    pytest's ``Captured Log``/``Captured Out``/``Captured Err`` headers are
+    added and before XML escaping, and is counted in Unicode characters, not
+    bytes, so multi-byte characters are never split. When a section's content
+    exceeds the limit, only its first N characters are kept and a fixed
+    truncation marker is appended (there is no retention of the end of the
+    content); the marker and the header do not count towards the limit. The
+    limit applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output
+    streams, but it never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic
+    text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``
+    and ``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering keep working unchanged.
+
+    This is **not** a cap on the overall size of a ``<system-out>``/
+    ``<system-err>`` element or of the XML file: it only bounds each raw
+    captured section before the header, truncation marker and full failure
+    tracebacks are added, so the final written content can still exceed the
+    configured number of characters.
+
+    Default is ``0``, which disables truncation and keeps the full captured
+    output, preserving the behavior from previous pytest versions (zero means
+    unlimited). Setting it to a negative or non-integer value is a
+    configuration error. Opt in by setting it to a positive number of
+    characters:
+
+    .. code-block:: ini
+
+        [pytest]
+        junit_logging = all
+        junit_output_limit = 2000
+
+

@@ -61,6 +61,36 @@ def bin_xml_escape(arg: object) -> str:
     return re.sub(illegal_xml_re, repl, str(arg))
 
 
+_TRUNCATION_MARKER = "\n[... output truncated ...]\n"
+
+
+def _truncate_content(content: str, limit: int) -> str:
+    """Truncate ``content`` to at most ``limit`` characters, keeping the start.
+
+    Operates on Unicode code points rather than bytes, so multi-byte
+    characters are never split. The appended marker does not count towards
+    ``limit``.
+    """
+    if limit <= 0 or len(content) <= limit:
+        return content
+    return content[:limit] + _TRUNCATION_MARKER
+
+
+def _parse_output_limit(value: str) -> int:
+    """Parse and validate the ``junit_output_limit`` ini value."""
+    try:
+        limit = int(value)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise pytest.UsageError(
+            f"junit_output_limit must be an integer, got {value!r}"
+        ) from None
+    if limit < 0:
+        raise pytest.UsageError(
+            f"junit_output_limit must be a non-negative integer, got {limit}"
+        )
+    return limit
+

index 000000000..25644eece
--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog/13802.feature.rst
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+Added a new :confval:`junit_output_limit` ini option (default ``0``, disabled) to limit how many Unicode characters of captured output (stdout, stderr, log) are kept per test and per section when writing the JUnit XML report. This helps avoid huge CI report uploads for test suites that print or log a lot.
+
+When enabled (e.g. ``junit_output_limit = 2000``), each raw captured section exceeding the limit is truncated to its first N Unicode characters (never splitting a multi-byte character) with a fixed truncation marker appended, before pytest's own headers are added -- this is a per-section character limit, not a byte or total file-size cap, so the header, marker and full failure tracebacks can still push the final written content past N characters. Truncation applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output, and never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``/``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering and configurations without this option (the default ``0`` means unlimited) are unaffected, as the feature is opt-in.

decisions.answer: I want a few changes. Call the ini setting junit_output_limit. Default 0 means unlimited. Positive values keep the first N Unicode code points of each raw captured stdout, stderr and log section independently, before adding headers or XML escaping. If cut, append a newline, [... output truncated ...], then a newline; the marker and header do not count toward N. No tail retention. Apply this equally to passing and failing tests' captured streams. Preserve the complete failure/error traceback diagnostics, and preserve existing junit_logging and junit_log_passing_tests filtering. Reject negative and non-integer settings with a clear configuration error. This keeps CI output bounded without hiding why a test failed.
